name: Beijing
tagline: 1864 Peking duck, reinvented with a Michelin star at the table next door.

Quanjude.description: China's most famous lacquered duck, roasted in a jujube-wood oven since 1864.

Dadong.description: A modern reinvention of Peking duck, with crispy skin and fine-dining presentation. Michelin star.

Haiwanju.description: Hand-pulled zhajiangmian noodles and traditional Beijing snacks. One of food writer Fuchsia Dunlop's personal favorites.

Najia Xiaoguan.description: Imperial Manchu cuisine from the Na family, descendants of Qing nobility, with recipes dating to 1748.

Li Qun Roast Duck.description: Peking duck in a hidden hutong courtyard, run by the same family for more than two decades. Anthony Bourdain's secret favorite on "No Reservations."

TRB Hutong.description: Contemporary French fine dining served in the courtyard of a former Buddhist temple near the Forbidden City. One Michelin star since the guide's Beijing debut.

King's Joy.description: Buddhist vegetarian fine dining in a courtyard house next to the Yonghegong Lama Temple. The world's first vegetarian restaurant to earn three Michelin stars.

Xin Rong Ji (Xinyuan South Road).description: Taizhou-style cooking built around fresh East China Sea seafood and a pre-order 28-day baby Peking duck. It was the first restaurant in Beijing to earn three Michelin stars.

Jing Yaa Tang.description: Wood-fired Peking duck and refined Cantonese cooking inside The Opposite House hotel in Sanlitun. One Michelin star.

Made in China.description: Jujube-wood-fired Peking duck and home-style northern Chinese classics inside the Grand Hyatt Beijing, recognized in the Beijing Michelin Guide.

1949 Duck de Chine.description: Peking duck roasted with Franco-Chinese technique inside a former factory complex reborn in 1949, tucked behind Sanlitun. Selected by the Beijing Michelin Guide.

Fangshan Restaurant.description: Qing-dynasty imperial cuisine served in historic pavilions on Qiongdao Island inside Beihai Park. Founded in 1925 by former court chefs.

Tan Family Cuisine.description: Tanjiacai cuisine, created by Qing-dynasty official Tan Zongjun to entertain senior officials and preserved since 1958 inside the historic Beijing Hotel at Premier Zhou Enlai's suggestion.

Donglaishun.description: Beijing's hot pot institution, founded in 1903 by Ding Deshan next to the old Dong'an Market. The benchmark for hand-cut lamb and the copper hot pot.

Jubaoyuan.description: Halal lamb hot pot in Niujie, Beijing's Muslim quarter, with roots in a halal butcher shop founded in 1937.

Bianyifang.description: The oldest surviving Peking duck restaurant, tracing back to 1416. It uses the 'menlu' method, roasting the duck inside a closed oven with no open flame.

Siji Minfu (Forbidden City).description: Hugely popular Peking duck spot next to the Forbidden City's Donghua Gate, with queues that can top a thousand tables during peak holidays.

Baodu Feng.description: Instantly scalded lamb and beef tripe, a recipe created in 1888 by Feng Lishan near the Houmen bridge. Now run by the seventh generation of the family.

Yaoji Chaogan.description: Chaogan (liver and tripe stewed in garlicky broth) at an eatery near the Drum Tower since 1989. US Vice President Joe Biden's 2011 visit brought it international fame.

Jiumen Xiaochi.description: A snack-food court under one roof gathering eleven historic vendors displaced from Qianmen by the urban renewal ahead of the 2008 Olympics.

Wangfujing Snack Street.description: A night market famous for its extreme skewers -scorpion, starfish, centipede- alongside traditional sweets like candied hawthorn tanghulu.

Hu Da Restaurant.description: The temple of spicy crayfish on Ghost Street (Guijie), open nearly around the clock with constant queues for more than two decades.

Liubiju Pickle and Sauce Shop.description: A pickle and sauce shop founded in 1530, the oldest in Beijing. Anthony Bourdain sampled its imperial pickled vegetables on 'No Reservations'.

Sculpting in Time.description: The literary cafe that opened in 1997 next to Peking University's east gate, two years before Beijing's first Starbucks arrived.

Metal Hands Coffee.description: A pioneer of specialty coffee in a Dongcheng hutong, famous for its 'Dirty Coffee'. The only mainland China cafe to make Big 7 Travel's world ranking.

Jing-A Brewing Co.description: A brewery founded in 2012 by two expats who had lived in Beijing for a decade, a pioneer in using Chinese ingredients like red rice koji and Sichuan peppercorn.

Capital Spirits Baijiu Bar & Distillery.description: The world's first bar dedicated entirely to baijiu, set inside a restored hutong shophouse. Featured by The New York Times in its 36 Hours in Beijing guide.

Apothecary.description: A speakeasy-style cocktail bar opened in 2009 by bartender Leon Lee, a benchmark of Beijing's craft cocktail scene with house syrups, bitters and hand-carved ice.

Great Leap Brewing.description: Beijing's first microbrewery, opened in 2010 inside a former siheyuan courtyard house near Nanluoguxiang. A pioneer of Chinese craft beer.

Xiao Wang Fu.description: Home-style Beijing cooking -duck, kung pao chicken, braised pork- a favorite of diplomats and expats for decades.

Bei.description: Northern Asian cuisine with touches of sushi and Peking duck, in a modernist interior designed by studio Neri&Hu inside The Opposite House hotel.

Migas Mercado.description: A rooftop gastro-market of Spanish tapas with views over the Sanlitun skyline, hand-carved Iberian ham and live music.

Crescent Moon Muslim Restaurant.description: Uyghur cuisine from Xinjiang -grilled lamb skewers, hand-pulled noodles, nang bread- in a Dongcheng hutong. Voted Beijing's best Xinjiang restaurant by The Beijinger's readers.

Middle 8th.description: One of the earliest Yunnan-cuisine restaurants near Sanlitun, known for its banana-leaf-wrapped fish and wild mushroom dishes.

Cafe Sambal.description: Malaysian Peranakan cooking in a hutong courtyard house since 2001, with spices flown in from Malaysia and Malaysian chefs in the kitchen.

Dali Courtyard.description: A seasonally changing multi-course set menu of Yunnan cuisine, served in a hutong courtyard tucked well away from the tourist routes.

Din Tai Fung.description: Beijing branch of the celebrated Taiwanese chain, famous for its eighteen-fold xiaolongbao and recommended by numerous international food critics.

Xibei Youmian Village.description: A chain born in Beijing in 1999, specializing in oat noodles and lamb from northwestern China, founded by entrepreneur Jia Guolong.

Home Plate BBQ.description: Slow-smoked Southern-style barbecue -brisket, ribs, pastrami- that began as a home delivery service before opening its first restaurant in Sanlitun.

Kong Yiji.description: A restaurant named after Lu Xun's short story, devoted to Shaoxing cuisine: drunken shrimp, Dongpo pork and yellow rice wine.
